title: Memory Is The Lynchpin Of The IT Industry, And Doubly So For AI
gist: Timothy Prickett Morgan argues memory has displaced compute as the control point of IT, with Gartner showing semiconductor revenue nearly doubling between 2025 and 2026 and DDR5 server memory costing 9X to 13X more than in November 2022. He expects HBM makers to lift HBM4E pricing in 2027 and GPU designers to trade HBM capacity for custom base dies and bandwidth.

insights.claim: Memory has come front and center and has eclipsed compute as the control point in most of the IT sector, a reversal of five decades in which CPUs and then GPUs were the focal point.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Value and pricing power in the AI stack are shifting toward memory suppliers.
insights.quote: memory has come front and center and has eclipsed compute as the control point in most of the IT sector
insights.locator: With the advent of machine learning

insights.claim: Gartner's chip revenue breakdown shows the semiconductor market nearly doubling between 2025 and 2026, with forecasts showing growth decelerating between 2026 and 2027, which the author says was inevitable as competition and sufficient capacity arrive.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Peak growth rate may be passing even as levels stay high.

insights.claim: The author estimates implied non-HBM DRAM revenues (DDR4, DDR5, LPDDR) will dwarf HBM sales for the foreseeable future, using Gartner growth rates and Micron's HBM TAM forecast.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Commodity DRAM, not just HBM, is the bigger profit pool in the memory upcycle.

insights.claim: Demand for DRAM, HBM and flash is boosted by GenAI and also by a server upgrade cycle replacing five-to-seven-year-old fleets, while the drive for core density to save space and power increases demand for high-capacity DRAM and flash.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Memory demand has a non-AI cyclical leg, which supports pricing beyond GenAI.

insights.claim: DRAM supplies are tightening as memory makers shift DRAM capacity to HBM for AI accelerators, chasing higher revenues but not necessarily higher profits, and traditional IT competes with tech titans for supply.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: HBM mix shift constrains conventional DRAM supply and supports commodity prices.

insights.claim: Hyperscalers and cloud builders have contracted the vast majority of disk drive supplies from Seagate, Western Digital and Toshiba, the three remaining disk drive makers.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Storage shortage extends from memory and flash to nearline disk.

insights.claim: Since November 2022, street prices of server DDR4 are up 2X to 3X, DDR5 up 9X to 13X, and a 30 TB TLC enterprise SSD up 6X to 7X, from baselines of roughly $3 per GB, $4 per GB and 10-13 cents per GB.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Server BOM costs have inflated sharply, squeezing buyers and boosting memory makers.
insights.quote: DDR5 server memory is anywhere from 9X to 13X higher

insights.claim: A 30 TB nearline disk drive costs about 2.5X more than in November 2022.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Even cheap bulk storage is inflating.

insights.claim: Part of the price change reflects the baseline: a memory and flash price crash in late 2021 from oversupply, which has plagued the industry for decades.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The starting point was cyclically depressed, so the multiples overstate underlying inflation.

insights.claim: HBM is sold in a closed market by three makers, Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron, to Nvidia, AMD and XPU makers, so there are no spot prices and pricing is rumored: about $20 per GB for HBM2 in 2017, about $8 two years later, $10 for HBM2E, $12 for HBM3, $13.50 for HBM3E, and about $16 for HBM4.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: HBM price per GB has been fairly stable, in contrast to commodity DRAM.

insights.claim: Nvidia's rumored HBM4 contract price is $560 to $600 per 36 GB stack, and finished HBM cost per GB is only up 1.6X since the GenAI boom started.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: HBM is cheap relative to commodity DRAM inflation, leaving room for price hikes.

insights.claim: The author doubts rumors that HBM4E will cost twice as much per GB as HBM4, seeing about $20 per GB as plausible but $36 per GB as tough to fathom, though HBM makers may raise HBM4E prices in 2027 to bring profitability closer to standard DRAM.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Expect an HBM4E price step-up but less than the most aggressive rumors.

insights.claim: HBM probably represents half the cost to users of an Nvidia or AMD GPU and closer to 65 percent for an XPU built by hyperscalers, cloud builders or model builders, now that OpenAI has entered with its 'Jalapeno' accelerator.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Memory is the majority of accelerator cost, so HBM pricing largely determines accelerator margins.

insights.claim: GPU and XPU makers are trying to do more with allocated HBM: some stick with more stacks of HBM3E instead of HBM4 to keep bandwidth for inference decode while sacrificing capacity.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: HBM scarcity is shaping product specs, which can cap per-device memory growth.

insights.claim: Nvidia is rumored to be backing away from the initial 'Rubin Ultra' plan of four reticle-limited chiplets and up to 1 TB of HBM4E, AMD is holding at 488 GB for the MI455X, and Nvidia may go as low as 192 GB on some future Rubin designs.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Roadmap capacity cuts would temper HBM unit demand growth.
insights.locator: Nvidia is rumored to be backing away

insights.claim: Nvidia's NVHBM moves the memory controller into a custom HBM base die; Nvidia says it delivers up to 30 percent greater memory bandwidth, 15 percent lower HBM power, and frees up to 25 percent more compute die area versus standard HBM4E, and others will follow with custom base dies, some with processing-in-memory functions.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Custom base dies move value to HBM packaging and logic and raise memory-vendor customization.
insights.quote: NVHBM delivers up to 30 percent greater memory bandwidth and 15 percent lower HBM power consumption
insights.locator: Here is why these custom base dies

insights.claim: The author predicts Rubin Ultra will use the freed area to use two chiplets and perhaps deliver 512 GB of HBM4E, or 384 GB at the same bandwidth, versus the original 1,024 GB and 58 TB/sec, maintaining about 28 TB/sec of bandwidth.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: If correct, HBM bits per accelerator drop roughly half versus the original plan.
